openClinicalQuestions: Which higher-dose (5 mg) folic acid indications does Dr. Charmi want listed for Indian readers beyond WHO’s previous NTD-affected pregnancy criterion—e.g. diabetes, haemoglobinopathies, epilepsy or HIV medicines as on the NHS UK list?

claimLedger.claim: 400 micrograms daily ideally 3 months before pregnancy or as soon as pregnant, until 12 weeks; difficult to get enough from food alone; prescribed 5 mg for listed UK risk groups
claimLedger.sourceSection: NHS · Pregnancy vitamins and supplements · Media last reviewed: 2 February 2026
claimLedger.limitations: UK higher-dose indication list; Indian clinicians may apply a different risk set

claimLedger.claim: 400 mcg folic acid daily preconception through first trimester
claimLedger.sourceSection: India National Health Mission · Anaemia Mukt Bharat · not stated; confirmed in operational guidelines PDF
claimLedger.limitations: Public-health tablet programme; does not itself list every 5 mg indication

claimLedger.claim: 400 μg from trying until 12 weeks; offer 5 mg after previous NTD-affected pregnancy
claimLedger.sourceSection: WHO · Periconceptional folic acid supplementation to prevent neural tube defects (eLENA) · last updated 9 Aug 2023 (parent-verified; live fetch timed out — search extract matched)
claimLedger.limitations: WHO high-dose wording centres on prior NTD pregnancy; other risk groups are jurisdiction-specific
